newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kyokuichi to make friendly bid for Yahagi Iron.
newsitem.headline: Kyokuichi to make friendly bid for Yahagi Iron.

text.p: Entertainment company Kyokuichi Corp will make a friendly takeover bid for Yahagi Iron Co Ltd as part of a broad tie-up, the companies said in a statement on Thursday.
The two companies said that they would consider starting the joint production of digital-image software.
Kyokuichi is 18.0 percent owned by Sega Enterprises Ltd.
On the planned share transfer, the two companies said Kyokuichi and its related parties would buy 15.65 million Yahagi shares from Yahagi's major shareholder, unlisted Kyoei Steel.
As a result, Kyokuichi and its related parties will own 47.93 percent in Yahagi, they said.
Kyoei Steel currently owns 16.65 million shares, or 50.99 percent, of Yahagi, the companies said.
Kyokuichi and Yahagi did not say when the planned share transfer would start, and declined to elaborate on other details.
Kyokuichi and Yahagi said joint businesses will include production of various movie and animation software titles, and the distribution of foreign-made software.
They may also aim to enter the satellite broadcasting and cable television businesses in the future, they said.
Despite the business and equity deal with Kyokuichi, Yahagi will also maintain its operations as a steel maker, continuing business ties with Kyoei Steel, the statement said.
